title: Electro-Pneumatic Actuator Sequencing and Pressure Regulation

content.aim: To design, wire, and evaluate a multi-cylinder electro-pneumatic automated sequence (A+ B+ A- B-) utilizing 5/2-way directional control valves with magnetic proximity sensor feedback.
objectives: To analyze the operating principles, force output, and flow-pressure dynamics of double-acting pneumatic cylinders.
To implement relay-based electrical interlocking circuits to eliminate pneumatic signal overlap.
To measure actuation stroke times under varying system pressures (2 to 6 bar) and exhaust throttle settings.
apparatus: Pneumatic training test bench with slotted profile plate
Double-acting pneumatic cylinders with magnetic pistons
V DC industrial relay module and push-button station
Air service unit (Filter-Regulator-Lubricator FRL unit) with pressure gauge
mm polyurethane pneumatic tubing and optical tachometer

theory.text: Pneumatic automation utilizes compressed air as a fluid power transmission medium to achieve rapid linear and rotary mechanical actuation. In double-acting cylinders, pressurized air applied to the advance port generates an extension force F = P × A_piston, while the retraction force is reduced by the piston rod cross-sectional area F_retract = P × (A_piston - A_rod). Electro-pneumatic control interfaces 24V DC low-voltage electrical signals with high-pressure pneumatic lines using solenoid-actuated spool valves. This hybrid architecture eliminates signal delay over long distances, isolates high pneumatic forces from operator controls, and enables seamless integration with microcontrollers and industrial automation controllers.

procedure: Connect the air service unit to the main compressor line and adjust the pressure regulator to 4.0 bar.
Mount the two double-acting cylinders (Cylinder A and Cylinder B) horizontally on the slotted profile plate.
Fit magnetic reed sensors at the retracted (A0, B0) and extended (A1, B1) limit positions of both cylinders.
Pipe the pneumatic lines between the 5/2-way double-solenoid valves and the cylinder ports using 4mm tubing.
Wire the 24V DC relay control circuit according to the cascaded sequence logic: Start button triggers A+, A1 triggers B+, B1 triggers A-, and A0 triggers B-.
Measure the extension and retraction times for both cylinders across supply pressures from 2.0 bar to 6.0 bar in 1.0 bar increments.
precautions: Always exhaust residual compressed air from the manifold before disconnecting pneumatic push-in fittings.
Ensure all magnetic proximity sensors are securely fastened to avoid signal chatter caused by cylinder end-stop impact vibrations.
Keep hands completely clear of cylinder stroke paths during continuous cycling tests.
content.discussion: The experimental results demonstrate an inverse non-linear relationship between supply pressure and total cycle completion time. As the system pressure increased from 2.0 to 6.0 bar, the extension time of Cylinder A decreased from 0.85s to 0.31s due to the higher volumetric flow rate through the 5/2 valve orifices. The meter-out flow control valves effectively eliminated piston stick-slip behavior during low-pressure strokes, ensuring smooth velocity transitions throughout the cascaded sequence. Minor timing discrepancies between cylinders A and B were attributed to differential tubing lengths causing slight pressure line drops.
content.conclusion: The electro-pneumatic cascaded motion sequence A+ B+ A- B- was successfully constructed and validated. Signal overlap was completely eliminated using electrical relay interlocking, achieving a minimum repeat cycle duration of 1.28 seconds at 6.0 bar rated operating pressure.
